teaser.text: Royal Caribbean Group sells vacations built around ships that carry guests, feed them, entertain them, and take them between destinations. Its business is a chain of advance bookings and onboard spending, followed by the costs of operating, maintaining, and financing those ships and the places they visit.

blocks.heading: Where could Royal Caribbean Group's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted forecast rises from $300.84 in October 2027 to $383.43 in October 2029, including dividends. That represents returns of 10% and 44% from today’s $277.62.

The range is much wider: by October 2029, the bear case gives $133.20 while the bull case gives $625.74. The forecast assigns the base case the highest probability because current demand and management guidance support growth, but debt, fixed costs and investment leave substantial downside.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Royal Caribbean Group, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The October 27, 2026 results test yields, costs and adjusted EPS against guidance as capacity grows. In 2027, Celebrity River Cruises must attract durable demand, and the Sandals and Beaches investment must add earnings at an adequate return. Longer term, new ships and destinations must lift cash earnings enough to fund commitments and reduce net debt without sacrificing returns. The case works only if growth converts into cash.

blocks.heading: How does Royal Caribbean Group make cash after stock pay?

paragraphs.text: Costa Maya illustrates the point. RCL paid $294 million for the port and adjacent land in 2025. Removing that purchase would reduce capital spending to $4,935 million and raise free cash flow to $1,530 million, but the result would still be below 2024. After treating stock compensation as an economic cost, analytical “real” free cash flow was $1,061 million.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Royal Caribbean Group today?

paragraphs.text: Cash provides the harder test. Royal Caribbean generated $6.5 billion of operating cash flow in 2025, but expected about $4.7 billion of capital expenditure in 2026, mainly for ships and destinations. Earnings can look strong while cash remains thin because a profitable fleet still needs replacement and expansion. The snapshot’s free-cash-flow yield was 1.7%, while its “real” free-cash-flow yield was 1.4%; that second calculation is not defined.

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $300.84 by October 2027. That implies a +10% return including dividends. It reaches $383.43 by October 2029. That implies a +44% return including dividends. The bear case has 28% probability. Base and bull have 52% and 20%, respectively. Real free cash flow per share fell to $3.87 even as diluted EPS rose to $15.61. blocks.heading: What could change Royal Caribbean Group's dividend?

paragraphs.text: Dividends begin at $6 per share in the base case, matching the current annualized quarterly rate, then rise to $6.50 and $7. The bear case cuts them to $4.50, $3 and zero as liquidity takes priority; the bull reaches $7.50 and $9 as earnings and cash generation strengthen. RCL has no predetermined dividend schedule, and shareholder payments already exceeded free cash flow in 2025.

blocks.heading: What is Royal Caribbean Group's dividend yield against its share price?

paragraphs.text: At October 16, 2026, one share cost $277.62. Market capitalization values the shares alone, while enterprise value adds debt and subtracts cash because lenders have claims before shareholders. Royal Caribbean reported $21.9 billion of debt and $825 million of cash at December 31, 2025. The difference is like buying a house with a mortgage: the house has value, but the owner’s equity comes after the bank is paid.

Cash provides the harder test. Royal Caribbean generated $6.5 billion of operating cash flow in 2025, but expected about $4.7 billion of capital expenditure in 2026, mainly for ships and destinations. Earnings can look strong while cash remains thin because a profitable fleet still needs replacement and expansion. The snapshot’s free-cash-flow yield was 1.7%, while its “real” free-cash-flow yield was 1.4%; that second calculation is not defined.

earnings.meta_description: Royal Caribbean Group reports on October 27, 2026; guidance points to higher yields and earnings as capacity grows.
earnings.opening: Royal Caribbean Group's next results are due on October 27, 2026. For Royal Caribbean Group, watch whether costs meet the promised decline as capacity grows.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Royal Caribbean Group's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Royal Caribbean Group guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: Royal Caribbean’s July 28 outlook calls for 2026 adjusted earnings per share of $17.73–$17.87, up 14%, against capacity growth of 6.6%. Adjusted earnings per share is profit divided among the shares, after management removes specified items. The gap means the plan relies on pricing, onboard spending, cost control and financing as well as fleet growth.

The company measures capacity in available passenger cruise days, or APCDs. A seven-night sailing with 1,000 two-person berths creates 7,000 APCDs whether every berth sells or not. Net yield is adjusted revenue after important selling and onboard costs, measured per APCD. Management expects full-year net yields to rise 1.8%–2.3% at constant currency while nonfuel costs per APCD remain flat. In plain terms, each available berth should earn more while costing no more to operate.

blocks.heading: Has Royal Caribbean Group kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: RCL announced that all three targets had been achieved eighteen months early, on a trailing-twelve-month basis. The resulting performance share unit award paid 298% of target. That means executives received 2.98 times the target share award; it does not mean the stock rose 298%. The achievement shows delivery, but the recovery of cruising also helped produce it.

blocks.heading: What have Royal Caribbean Group's last eight quarters shown?

paragraphs.text: Profit lagged revenue. Gross margin fell from 40.5% to 37.7%, and operating income declined from $1,329 million to $1,307 million. Net income fell from $1,210 million to $1,128 million, while diluted EPS declined from $4.41 to $4.20.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Royal Caribbean Group's next results?

paragraphs.text: Royal Caribbean’s next dated test is October 27, 2026. Investors will compare yield with the flat outlook, adjusted EPS with guidance and analyst expectations, and costs with the promised decline. Revenue growth alone will not settle the question because more berths can produce more sales even when each berth earns no more.
